subtopics.title: Types of number
objectives: Identify and use natural numbers (0, 1, 2, ...)
Identify and use integers (positive, zero and negative)
Identify and use prime numbers
Identify and use square numbers
Identify and use cube numbers
Identify and use triangle numbers
Identify and use common factors
Identify and use common multiples
Identify and use rational and irrational numbers
Identify and use reciprocals

notes_and_examples.text: Example tasks include: convert between numbers and words, e.g. six billion is 6000000000, 10007 is ten thousand and seven; express 72 as a product of its prime factors; find the highest common factor (HCF) of two numbers; find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of two numbers.

subtopics.title: Sets
objectives: Understand and use set language, notation and Venn diagrams to describe sets and represent relationships between sets.

notes_and_examples.text:
Venn diagrams are limited to two or three sets.
Set notation used:
- Number of elements in set A: $n(A)$
- Element of: $\in$
- Not an element of: $\notin$
- Complement of set A: $A'$
- The empty set: $\emptyset$
- Universal set: $\mathcal{U}$
- Subset: $A \subseteq B$
- Not a subset: $A \nsubseteq B$
- Union: $A \cup B$
- Intersection: $A \cap B$
Example definition of sets:
$A = \{x | x \text{ is a natural number}\}$
$B = \{(x,y) | y = mx+c\}$
$C = \{x | a \le x \le b\}$
$D = \{a, b, c, ...\}$

subtopics.title: Powers and roots
objectives: Calculate with squares, square roots, cubes, cube roots, and other powers and roots of numbers.

notes_and_examples.text:
Includes recall of squares and their corresponding roots from 1 to 15, and recall of cubes and their corresponding roots of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10.
Examples: Write down the value of $\sqrt{169}$. Work out $5^2 \times \sqrt[3]{8}$.

subtopics.title: Fractions, decimals and percentages
objectives: Use the language and notation of proper fractions, improper fractions, mixed numbers, decimals, and percentages in appropriate contexts.
Recognise equivalence and convert between these forms.

notes_and_examples.text: Candidates are expected to be able to write fractions in their simplest form.

subtopics.title: Ordering
objectives: Order quantities by magnitude and demonstrate familiarity with the symbols =, \neq, >, <, \ge, and \le.

subtopics.title: The four operations
objectives: Use the four operations for calculations with integers, fractions and decimals, including correct ordering of operations and use of brackets.

notes_and_examples.text: Includes negative numbers, improper fractions, mixed numbers, practical situations (e.g. temperature changes).

subtopics.title: Indices I
objectives: Understand and use indices (positive, zero, negative and fractional).
Understand and use the rules of indices.

subtopics.title: Standard form
objectives: Use the standard form $A \times 10^n$ where $n$ is a positive or negative integer and $1 \le A < 10$.
Convert numbers into and out of standard form.
Calculate with values in standard form.

subtopics.title: Estimation
objectives: Round values to a specified degree of accuracy.
Make estimates for calculations involving numbers, quantities and measurements.
Round answers to a reasonable degree of accuracy in the context of a given problem.

notes_and_examples.text:
Includes decimal places and significant figures.
e.g. Write 5764 correct to the nearest thousand.
e.g. By writing each number correct to 1 significant figure, estimate the value of $\frac{41.3}{9.79 \times 0.765}$.

subtopics.title: Ratio and proportion
objectives: Understand and use ratio and proportion to: give ratios in their simplest form; divide a quantity in a given ratio; use proportional reasoning and ratios in context.

notes_and_examples.text:
e.g. 20:30:40 in its simplest form is 2:3:4.
e.g. adapt recipes; use map scales; determine best value.

subtopics.title: Rates
objectives: Use common measures of rate.
Solve problems involving average speed.

notes_and_examples.text:
Calculate with hourly rates of pay, exchange rates, flow rates, fuel consumption.
Knowledge of speed/distance/time formula is required.
e.g. A cyclist travels 45 km in 3 hours 45 minutes. What is their average speed?
Notation used: $m/s$, $g/cm^3$.

subtopics.title: Percentages
objectives: Calculate a given percentage of a quantity.
Express one quantity as a percentage of another.
Calculate percentage increase or decrease.
Calculate with simple and compound interest.
Calculate using reverse percentages.

notes_and_examples.text:
Problems may include repeated percentage change. Formulas are not given.
e.g. find the cost price given the selling price and the percentage profit.
Percentage calculations may include: deposit, discount, profit and loss (as amount or percentage), earnings, percentages over 100%.

subtopics.title: Using a calculator
objectives: Use a calculator efficiently.
Enter values appropriately on a calculator.
Interpret the calculator display appropriately.

notes_and_examples.text:
Know not to round values within a calculation and to only round the final answer.
e.g. enter 2 hours 30 minutes as 2.5 hours or $2^\circ 30' 0''$.
e.g. in money 4.8 means $4.80; in time 3.25 means 3 hours 15 minutes.

subtopics.title: Time
objectives: Calculate with time: seconds (s), minutes (min), hours (h), days, weeks, months, years, including the relationship between units.
Calculate times in terms of the 24-hour and 12-hour clock.
Read clocks and timetables.

notes_and_examples.text:
1 year = 365 days.
24-hour clock: 3.15 a.m. is 03 15 and 3.15 p.m. is 15 15.
Includes problems involving time zones, local times and time differences.

subtopics.title: Money
objectives: Calculate with money.
Convert from one currency to another.

subtopics.title: Exponential growth and decay
objectives: Use exponential growth and decay.

notes_and_examples.text: e.g. depreciation, population change. Knowledge of e is not required.

subtopics.title: Surds
objectives: Understand and use surds, including simplifying expressions.
Rationalise the denominator.

notes_and_examples.text:
Examples include:
$\sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}$
$\sqrt{200} - \sqrt{32} = 6\sqrt{2}$
$\frac{10}{\sqrt{5}} = 2\sqrt{5}$
$\frac{1}{-1+\sqrt{3}} = \frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{2}$

subtopics.title: Introduction to algebra
objectives: Know that letters can be used to represent generalised numbers.
Substitute numbers into expressions and formulas.

subtopics.title: Algebraic manipulation
objectives: Simplify expressions by collecting like terms.
Expand products of algebraic expressions.
Factorise by extracting common factors.
Factorise expressions of specified forms.

notes_and_examples.text:
Forms to factorise: $ax+bx+kay+kby$, $a^2x^2-b^2y^2$, $a^2+2ab+b^2$, $ax^2+bx+c$, $ax^3+bx^2+cx$.
Simplify means simplest form, e.g. $2a^2+3ab-1+5a^2-9ab+4 = 7a^2-6ab+3$.
Expand e.g. $3x(2x-4y)$, $(3x+y)(x-4y)$, $(3x+4)^2$, $(x-2)(x+3)(2x+1)$.
Factorise fully e.g. $9x^2+15xy = 3x(3x+5y)$.

subtopics.title: Algebraic fractions
objectives: Manipulate algebraic fractions.
Factorise and simplify rational expressions.

notes_and_examples.text:
Examples include:
$\frac{x}{3}+\frac{x-4}{2}$, $\frac{2x}{3}-\frac{3(x-5)}{2}$, $\frac{3a}{4}\times\frac{9a}{10}$, $\frac{3a}{4}\div\frac{9a}{10}$, $\frac{1}{x-2}+\frac{x+1}{x-3}$, $\frac{x^2-2x}{x^2-5x+6}$.

subtopics.title: Indices II
objectives: Understand and use indices (positive, zero, negative and fractional).
Understand and use the rules of indices.

subtopics.title: Equations
objectives: Construct expressions, equations and formulas.
Solve linear equations in one unknown.
Solve fractional equations with numerical and linear algebraic denominators.
Solve simultaneous linear equations in two unknowns.
Solve quadratic equations by factorisation, using a graphic display calculator and by use of the quadratic formula.
Change the subject of formulas.
Use a graphic display calculator to solve equations, including those which may be unfamiliar.

notes_and_examples.text:
e.g. write expression for product of two consecutive even numbers.
Includes constructing simultaneous equations.
e.g. $3x+4=10$, $5-2x=3(x+7)$.
Fractional e.g. $\frac{x}{2x+1}=4$, $\frac{2}{x+2}+\frac{3}{2x-1}=1$, $\frac{x}{x+2}=\frac{3}{x-6}$.
Candidates may be expected to give solutions in surd form. Quadratic formula is given.
Change subject where subject appears twice or contains power/root.
GDC e.g. $2x-1 = \frac{1}{x^3}$.

subtopics.title: Inequalities
objectives: Represent and interpret inequalities, including on a number line.
Construct, solve and interpret linear inequalities.
Solve inequalities using a graphic display calculator.
Represent and interpret linear inequalities in two variables graphically.
List inequalities that define a given region.

notes_and_examples.text:
Number line: open circles for strict (<, >), closed circles for inclusive (<=, >=), e.g. $-3 \le x < 1$.
Linear examples: $3x < 2x+4$, $-3 \le 3x-2 < 7$.
Graphical conventions: broken lines for strict (<, >), solid lines for inclusive (<=, >=), shading for unwanted regions.

subtopics.title: Sequences
objectives: Continue a given number sequence or pattern.
Recognise patterns in sequences, including the term-to-term rule, and relationships between different sequences.
Find and use the nth term of sequences.

notes_and_examples.text:
Subscript notation may be used, e.g. $T_n$ is the nth term of sequence T.
Includes linear, quadratic, cubic and exponential sequences and simple combinations of these.
Includes use of a difference method to find the nth term for a linear, quadratic or cubic sequence.

subtopics.title: Proportion
objectives: Express direct and inverse proportion in algebraic terms and use this form of expression to find unknown quantities.
Identify the best variation model for given data.

notes_and_examples.text:
Includes linear, square, square root and cube proportion.
Knowledge of proportional symbol ($\propto$) is required.

subtopics.title: Graphs of functions
objectives: Recognise function types from graph shapes: linear $f(x)=ax+b$, quadratic $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$, cubic $f(x)=ax^3+bx^2+cx+d$, reciprocal $f(x)=\frac{a}{x}$, exponential $f(x)=a^x$ ($0<a<1$ or $a>1$), trigonometric $f(x)=a\sin(bx)$, $a\cos(bx)$, $\tan x$.
Determine one or two of a, b, c or d for the graphs above.
Determine values in a function from its graph.

notes_and_examples.text: Includes recognising symmetry, period, and amplitude. Some coefficients may be 0.

subtopics.title: Sketching graphs on a calculator
objectives: Use a graphic display calculator to: sketch the graph of a function, produce a table of values, plot points, find zeros, local maxima or local minima, find the intersection of the graphs of functions, find the vertex of a quadratic.

notes_and_examples.text: Includes unfamiliar functions not mentioned explicitly in the syllabus.

subtopics.title: Functions
objectives: Understand functions, domain and range and use function notation.
Understand and find inverse functions $f^{-1}(x)$.
Form composite functions as defined by $gf(x) = g(f(x))$.

notes_and_examples.text:
Examples: $f(x)=3x-5$, $g(x)=\frac{3(x+4)}{5}$, $h(x)=2x^2+3$.
e.g. $f(x)=\frac{3}{x+2}$ and $g(x)=(3x+5)^2$. Find $fg(x)$. Give answer as fraction in simplest form.
Candidates are not expected to find domain and range of composite functions. May include mapping diagrams.

subtopics.title: Finding a quadratic function using given information
objectives: Find a quadratic function given: vertex and another point; x-intercepts and a point; vertex or x-intercepts in the case where $a=1$.

notes_and_examples.text: $y = a(x-h)^2 + k$ has a vertex of $(h, k)$.

subtopics.title: Asymptotes
objectives: Understand the concept of asymptotes and identify simple examples parallel to the axes on a graph.

notes_and_examples.text:
e.g. $f(x)=\tan x$ has asymptotes at $90^\circ, 270^\circ, ...$
Excludes algebraic derivation of asymptotes.

subtopics.title: Transforming graphs of functions
objectives: Describe and identify transformations to a graph of $y=f(x)$ when $y=f(x)+k$ or $y=f(x+k)$.

notes_and_examples.text: e.g. graph $y=f(x)$ mapped onto $y=g(x)$ by translation with vector. Find $g(x)$ in terms of $x$, where $k$ is an integer.

subtopics.title: The logarithmic function
objectives: Understand and use the logarithmic function as the inverse of the exponential function.
Understand $y=a^x$ as equivalent to $x=\log_a y$.
Understand the solution to $a^x=b$ as $x=\frac{\log b}{\log a}$.

notes_and_examples.text:
All logs will be base 10 unless otherwise stated.
e.g. solve log equations in context of compound interest or exponential growth/decay.
e.g. solve a log equation from a graph or otherwise.

subtopics.title: Coordinates
objectives: Use and interpret Cartesian coordinates in two dimensions.

subtopics.title: Gradient of linear graphs
objectives: Find the gradient of a straight line.
Calculate the gradient of a straight line from the coordinates of two points on it.

subtopics.title: Length and midpoint
objectives: Calculate the length of a line segment.
Find the coordinates of the midpoint of a line segment.

subtopics.title: Equations of linear graphs
objectives: Interpret and obtain the equation of a straight-line graph.

notes_and_examples.text:
Forms include: $ax+by=c$, $y=mx+c$, $x=k$.
Involve finding equation given graph, or finding gradient/y-intercept from equation e.g. find gradient & y-intercept of $5x+4y=8$.
Equations must be given in fully simplified form.

subtopics.title: Parallel lines
objectives: Find the gradient and equation of a straight line parallel to a given line.

notes_and_examples.text: e.g. find equation of line parallel to $y=4x-1$ passing through $(1, -3)$.

subtopics.title: Perpendicular lines
objectives: Find the gradient and equation of a straight line perpendicular to a given line.

notes_and_examples.text:
e.g. find gradient of line perpendicular to $2y=3x+1$.
e.g. find equation of perpendicular bisector of line joining $(-3, 8)$ and $(9, -2)$.

subtopics.title: Geometrical terms
objectives: Use and interpret geometrical terms: point, vertex, line, plane, parallel, perpendicular, perpendicular bisector, bearing, right angle, acute, obtuse, reflex angles, interior and exterior angles, similar, congruent, scale factor.

Use and interpret vocabulary of triangles (equilateral, isosceles, scalene, right-angled), quadrilaterals (square, rectangle, kite, rhombus, parallelogram, trapezium), polygons (regular/irregular, pentagon, hexagon, octagon, decagon), solids (cube, cuboid, prism, cylinder, pyramid, tetrahedron, cone, sphere, hemisphere, frustum, face, surface, edge).
Use and interpret vocabulary of a circle: centre, radius/radii, diameter, circumference, semicircle, chord, tangent, major/minor arc, sector, segment.

notes_and_examples.text: Candidates are not expected to show that two shapes are congruent.

subtopics.title: Angle measurement in degrees
objectives: Measure and draw lines and angles.
Use and interpret three-figure bearings.

notes_and_examples.text:
Ruler must be used for straight edges.
Bearings measured clockwise from north ($000^\circ$ to $360^\circ$).
e.g. find bearing of A from B if bearing of B from A is $025^\circ$.
Understanding of cardinal directions e.g. point D is due east of point C.

subtopics.title: Similarity
objectives: Calculate lengths of similar shapes.
Use relationships between lengths, areas, surface areas, and volumes of similar shapes/solids: $\frac{\text{Volume A}}{\text{Volume B}} = \frac{(\text{Length A})^3}{(\text{Length B})^3}$.
Solve problems and give simple explanations involving similarity.

notes_and_examples.text: Includes showing two triangles are similar using geometric reasons.

subtopics.title: Symmetry
objectives: Recognise line symmetry and order of rotational symmetry in two dimensions.
Recognise symmetry properties of prisms, cylinders, pyramids and cones.

notes_and_examples.text:
Includes properties of triangles, quadrilaterals and polygons directly related to symmetries.
e.g. identify planes and axes of symmetry.

subtopics.title: Angles
objectives: Calculate unknown angles and give simple explanations using geometrical properties: sum at point = $360^\circ$, sum on line = $180^\circ$, vertically opposite, triangle sum = $180^\circ$, quadrilateral sum = $360^\circ$.
Calculate unknown angles and give geometric explanations for parallel lines: corresponding angles equal, alternate angles equal, co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$.
Know and use angle properties of regular and irregular polygons.

notes_and_examples.text:
Knowledge of three-letter notation required (e.g. angle $ABC$). Correct terminology expected.
Includes exterior and interior angles, and angle sum.

subtopics.title: Circle theorems I
objectives: Calculate unknown angles and give explanations using circle properties: angle in semicircle = $90^\circ$, tangent to radius = $90^\circ$, angle at centre is twice angle at circumference, angles in same segment equal, opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral sum to $180^\circ$, alternate segment theorem.

notes_and_examples.text: Candidates expected to use listed geometrical properties when giving reasons.

subtopics.title: Circle theorems II
objectives: Use symmetry properties of circles: equal chords are equidistant from centre, perpendicular bisector of chord passes through centre, tangents from external point equal in length.

notes_and_examples.text: Candidates expected to use listed geometrical properties when giving reasons.

subtopics.title: Units of measure
objectives: Use metric units of mass, length, area, volume and capacity in practical situations and convert quantities into larger or smaller units.

notes_and_examples.text:
Units: mm, cm, m, km, mm^2, cm^2, m^2, km^2, mm^3, cm^3, m^3, ml, l, g, kg.
Conversions include area ($cm^2 \leftrightarrow m^2$) and volume/capacity ($m^3 \leftrightarrow \text{litres}$).

subtopics.title: Area and perimeter
objectives: Carry out calculations involving perimeter and area of rectangle, triangle, parallelogram and trapezium.

notes_and_examples.text: Except for area of triangle, formulas are not given.

subtopics.title: Circles, arcs and sectors
objectives: Carry out calculations involving circumference and area of a circle.
Carry out calculations involving arc length and sector area as fractions of circumference and area.

notes_and_examples.text: Answers may be asked in terms of $\pi$. Formulas are given. Includes minor and major sectors.

subtopics.title: Surface area and volume
objectives: Carry out calculations and solve problems involving surface area and volume of: cuboid, prism, cylinder, sphere, pyramid, cone.

notes_and_examples.text:
Answers may be asked in terms of $\pi$.
Formulas given: curved surface area of cylinder/cone, surface area of sphere, volume of prism/pyramid/cylinder/cone/sphere.
Prism refers to any solid with uniform cross-section (e.g. cylindrical sector).

subtopics.title: Compound shapes and parts of shapes
objectives: Carry out calculations and solve problems involving perimeters and areas of compound shapes and parts of shapes.
Carry out calculations and solve problems involving surface areas and volumes of compound solids and parts of solids.

notes_and_examples.text:
Answers may be asked in terms of $\pi$.
e.g. find surface area and volume of a frustum.

subtopics.title: Pythagoras' theorem
objectives: Know and use Pythagoras' theorem.

notes_and_examples.text: Includes finding length of chord, distance of chord from centre of circle, distance between two points given on a grid.

subtopics.title: Right-angled triangles
objectives: Know and use sine, cosine and tangent ratios for acute angles in calculations involving sides and angles of a right-angled triangle.
Solve problems in two dimensions using Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometry.
Know that perpendicular distance from a point to a line is the shortest distance.
Carry out calculations involving angles of elevation and depression.

notes_and_examples.text: Angles given in degrees, answers in degrees correct to 1 d.p. Knowledge of bearings may be required.

subtopics.title: Exact trigonometric values
objectives: Know exact values of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$ for $x = 0^\circ, 30^\circ, 45^\circ, 60^\circ, 90^\circ$.
Know exact values of \tan x for $x = 0^\circ, 30^\circ, 45^\circ, 60^\circ$.

subtopics.title: Trigonometric functions
objectives: Recognise, sketch and interpret graphs for $0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ$: $y=\sin x$, $y=\cos x$, $y=\tan x$.
Solve trigonometric equations involving $\sin x$, $\cos x$ or $\tan x$ for $0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ$.

notes_and_examples.text:
e.g. solve $\sin x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ for $0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ$.
e.g. solve $2\cos x + 1 = 0$ for $0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ$.

subtopics.title: Non-right-angled triangles
objectives: Use sine and cosine rules in calculations involving lengths and angles for any triangle.
Use formula $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$.

notes_and_examples.text: Includes obtuse angles and ambiguous case. Sine/cosine rules and area formula are given.

subtopics.title: Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometry in 3D
objectives: Carry out calculations and solve problems in 3D using Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometry, including calculating the angle between a line and a plane.

subtopics.title: Transformations
objectives: Recognise, describe and draw reflection in a straight line.
Recognise, describe and draw rotation about a centre through multiples of $90^\circ$.
Recognise, describe and draw enlargement from a centre by a scale factor.
Recognise, describe and draw translation by a vector $\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix}$.

notes_and_examples.text:
Questions may involve combinations of transformations or reverse transformations.
Ruler must be used. Positive, fractional and negative scale factors may be used.

subtopics.title: Vectors in two dimensions
objectives: Describe a translation using a vector represented by $\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix}$, $\vec{AB}$ or $\mathbf{a}$.
Add and subtract vectors.
Multiply a vector by a scalar.

notes_and_examples.text: Vectors printed as $\vec{AB}$ or $\mathbf{a}$.

subtopics.title: Magnitude of a vector
objectives: Calculate the magnitude of a vector $\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix}$ as $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$.

notes_and_examples.text: Magnitudes denoted by modulus signs: $|\mathbf{a}|$ is magnitude of $\mathbf{a}$, $|\vec{AB}|$ is magnitude of $\vec{AB}$.

subtopics.title: Introduction to probability
objectives: Understand and use probability scale from 0 to 1.
Understand and use probability notation: $P(A)$, $P(A')$.
Calculate probability of a single event.
Understand that $P(\text{event not occurring}) = 1 - P(\text{event occurring})$.

notes_and_examples.text:
Probabilities as fraction, decimal or percentage.
May require information from tables, graphs or Venn diagrams.
e.g. $P(B)=0.8$, find $P(B')$.

subtopics.title: Relative and expected frequencies
objectives: Understand relative frequency as an estimate of probability.
Calculate expected frequencies.

notes_and_examples.text:
e.g. use results of spinner experiment to estimate probability.
e.g. use probability to estimate expected value from population.
Includes understanding fair, bias and random.

subtopics.title: Probability of combined events
objectives: Calculate probability of combined events using sample space diagrams, Venn diagrams, tree diagrams.

notes_and_examples.text:
Combined events with or without replacement.
Notation $P(A \cap B)$ and $P(A \cup B)$ in Venn diagrams.
Tree diagrams: outcomes at end of branches, probabilities on sides.
$P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B)$ for mutually exclusive.
$P(A \text{ and } B) = P(A) \times P(B)$ for independent.

subtopics.title: Classifying statistical data
objectives: Classify and tabulate statistical data.

notes_and_examples.text: e.g. tally tables, two-way tables.

subtopics.title: Interpreting statistical data
objectives: Read, interpret and draw inferences from tables and statistical diagrams.
Compare sets of data using tables, graphs and statistical measures.
Appreciate restrictions on drawing conclusions from given data.

notes_and_examples.text: e.g. compare averages and measures of spread between two data sets.

subtopics.title: Discrete and continuous data
objectives: Distinguish between discrete and continuous data.

subtopics.title: Averages and measures of spread
objectives: Calculate mean, median, mode, quartiles, range and interquartile range for individual data and distinguish between purposes.
Calculate an estimate of the mean for grouped discrete or grouped continuous data.
Identify the modal class from a grouped frequency distribution.

subtopics.title: Averages on a calculator
objectives: Use a graphic display calculator to calculate: mean, median and quartiles for discrete data; mean for grouped data.

subtopics.title: Statistical charts and diagrams
objectives: Draw and interpret: bar charts (composite/stacked, dual/side-by-side), pie charts, pictograms, stem-and-leaf diagrams, simple frequency distributions.

notes_and_examples.text: Stem-and-leaf diagrams should have ordered data with a key.

subtopics.title: Scatter diagrams
objectives: Draw and interpret scatter diagrams.
Understand positive, negative and zero correlation.
Draw by eye, interpret and use a straight line of best fit.
Use a graphic display calculator to find and use the equation of linear regression.

notes_and_examples.text:
Points marked clearly as small crosses (x).
Line of best fit: single ruled line through mean point, extends across full data set, roughly even distribution of points either side.

subtopics.title: Cumulative frequency diagrams
objectives: Draw and interpret cumulative frequency tables and diagrams.
Estimate and interpret median, percentiles, quartiles and interquartile range from cumulative frequency diagrams.

notes_and_examples.text: Points marked clearly as small crosses (x) and joined with a smooth curve.
